source.title: MixtureVitae: Open Web-Scale Pretraining Dataset With High Quality Instruction and Reasoning Data Built from Permissive-First Text Sources
source.authors: Huu Nguyen; Victor May; H. Raj; Marianna Nezhurina; Yi-Shan Wang; Yan-Qi Luo; Minh Chien Vu; Taishi Nakamura; Ken Tsui; V. Nguyen; David Salinas; Aleksandra Krasnodebska; Christoph Schuhmann; Mats Leon Richter; X. Vu; J. Jitsev

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training tokens and model size and reports downstream benchmark trajectories, but it does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss or fit the scaling laws in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports many downstream benchmark comparisons across datasets, including fixed-budget comparisons and data-component ablations. These do not test the claim versions unless they measure downstream performance as it varies with model size or training tokens. Results cited from other work are not recorded as study findings.
record.test_reason: This is a dataset paper. It compares downstream benchmark accuracy across pretraining corpora under a fixed protocol (open-sci-ref). It measures no held-out loss and fits no scaling relation. It never asks whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or loss. Token trajectories and model-size panels are shown only to rank datasets. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited for the 6N FLOP estimate and for per-budget learning-rate schedules, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a permissive-first corpus dense in instruction and reasoning data outperforms other permissive corpora and nears DCLM/FineWeb-Edu at 1.7B/300B. They add that instruction data drives most gains (ablation) and that the gains survive decontamination. They draw no scaling-law conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream task performance across data mixtures, token budgets, and model sizes under the open-sci-ref training protocol; it does not use held-out cross-entropy loss or fit parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that MixtureVitae’s relative performance depends on the benchmark, training-token budget, and model size; it does not analyze scaling-law fit sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: With architecture and hyperparameters fixed, downstream accuracy curves over training tokens differ in level and slope across corpora. MixtureVitae's advantage over permissive corpora is larger at 1.3B/1.7B than at 0.13B/0.4B. No fit is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data composition changes how downstream accuracy scales with tokens and model size (data-dependent downstream scaling).

record.problems: For the claim-relevant downstream trajectories, values are presented in plots without uncertainty estimates. The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss or perform predictive scaling-law fits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were kept from the fixed-budget dataset comparisons or data-component ablations: those do not vary model size or training tokens in a way that tests downstream predictability. The paper also reports many individual benchmark curves in Appendix C.1 and C.2; they were not extracted separately because the claim-relevant reported summaries are represented by R1–R3.

untested.parts: Architecture fixed per size; shape not varied at fixed parameters.
No scaling law fitted in other regimes.
Downstream accuracy curves over tokens and sizes are shown, but predictability from scale or loss is never fitted or tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 with a V6 limits_scope label overreads plain learning curves; the rows are recoded to none. The model-size panels (Fig. 8) carry no numeric values. Ablation and decontamination curves are also irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and several-orders-of-magnitude behavior.
Fitting laws on smaller runs and predicting loss on substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their relationship to compute.
Architectural variation at a fixed parameter count and its effect on loss.
Testing whether the same loss scaling law holds in other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports downstream benchmark trajectories, but does not test forecasts from scale or pretraining loss, or fit a predictive relationship.
Whether fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on setup and fitting choices, or whether loss curves bend away from power laws.

rows.subject: MixtureVitae (Ours), 1.7B-parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Reports average downstream accuracy over training tokens
rows.measure: Average downstream performance as a function of training tokens
rows.note: The text says MixtureVitae approaches FineWeb-Edu and DCLM toward the 300B-token budget, and that only Nemotron-CC-HQ catches up around 260B and overtakes it past that point. No fitted predictive relation is reported.
rows.check: Figure 3a is a dataset-ranking learning curve with no fit, forecast or loss relation, so it cannot show V6's predictability. The 'partial' state is unsupported. The value is figure-only.

rows.subject: MixtureVitae (Ours), 1.7B-parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Reports MMLU performance over training tokens
rows.measure: MMLU downstream performance as a function of training tokens
rows.note: The text says MixtureVitae performs particularly well on MMLU relative to the other datasets. The figure gives the token trajectory, but the paper does not fit or validate a prediction.
rows.check: Figure 3b is an MMLU trajectory used to compare datasets. There is no predictive relation to scale or loss, so V6 cannot be judged.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, MMLU discussion; Figure 3b and caption.

rows.subject: MixtureVitae models (aggregate across tested model sizes)
rows.operation_detail: Compares average downstream performance across model sizes at the 50B-token budget
rows.measure: Average downstream performance by model size
rows.note: The text describes an early, consistent lead over other permissive datasets, especially at the 1.3B and 1.7B scales. The figure presents results for four model sizes; no predictive scaling fit is reported.
rows.check: Figure 8 shows 50B-token trajectories at four sizes for permissive datasets only. It is a comparison of MixtureVitae's lead over other datasets, not a test of predictable improvement with scale. No numbers are given.

relation.reason: Section 3.1 cites Hoffmann et al. for budget-specific learning-rate schedules, without testing or applying the catalog's scaling-law claims.

tranche.reason: The study compares pretraining datasets using downstream benchmarks. Its token trajectories and model-size comparisons neither fit nor validate a scaling relation or predictive mapping, and it does not apply a scaling law as a tool.

source_check.notes: R1's note mentions Nemotron-CC-HQ catching up around 260B tokens; Section 3.2 attributes that crossover to MMLU (R2), not average performance. Figure 8 contains training trajectories at four sizes, rather than a fitted relation across sizes.
